summary: One controller for both top-down and simple 3D platformer movement, on Unity's CharacterController.
overview: Movement for two common cases from one component: turn gravity and jump off for top-down, on for a simple platformer. It sits on Unity's own CharacterController, so slopes and steps are handled properly rather than hand-rolled. Input comes through LegacyInputManager — one line in Update swaps it to the Input System version.
useCases: A top-down or isometric player that walks and faces its direction of travel.
A simple 3D platformer character without writing collision code.
A prototype player you expect to replace later, but need working now.

params.tuning: Off for top-down. With it off, jump is meaningless even if allowJump is ticked.
A height in metres, not an impulse, so it stays predictable when you change gravity.
Turn off for a character that should keep facing a target while strafing.

gotchas.title: The transform pivot is the capsule CENTRE, not the feet
gotchas.body: Unity's CharacterController defaults to centre (0,0,0) and height 2, which puts the pivot a full metre above the ground contact. Anything computing a height "above the feet" must derive it from center and height rather than assuming the pivot is at ground level.

gotchas.title: Kinematic, so it does not push rigidbodies
gotchas.body: CharacterController resolves collisions by sliding, not by physics. Pushing crates needs an OnControllerColliderHit of your own.
